english.title: Cause possession of stamp fraudulently printed, impressed, cut, torn, mutilated, erased or removed
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) caused **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to knowingly, and without lawful excuse, possess

(A)_[a stamp which had been fraudulently printed or impressed from a genuine die]_
(B)_[a stamp or part of a stamp which had been fraudulently cut, torn, or otherwise removed from material]_
(C)_[a stamp which had been fraudulently mutilated]_
(D)_[stamped material out of which a matter or thing, namely **(..SPECIFY MATTER OR THING..) had been fraudulently erased or otherwise removed]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 13(1), (2) and (9) of the Stamp Duties Management Act 1891.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
caused to be done
knowingly

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 13(9) of the Stamp Duties Management Act 1891 provides that it shall be for the defendant to prove that he had a lawful excuse.
(ii) The wording of section 13, and the definition of 'die', 'stamp' and 'stamped' in section 27, were amended on 22nd April 2019 to include stamps made by any machine, not just impressed stamps. From this date, see offence document H.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Ten years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
